You are an independent classifier in a blinded experiment about a book of
biblical symbolism. The consensus responses below were produced without access
to the book. Compare them with the book's entry.

TERM
Sabbath

BLIND CONSENSUS RESPONSES

{
  "primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching the Sabbath is most commonly interpreted symbolically as God's rest — a type or foreshadowing of the spiritual rest believers find in Christ and, ultimately, of the eschatological rest of the people of God (salvation rest / heavenly rest). The weekly Sabbath, grounded in God's rest at creation, is read as pointing beyond itself to ceasing from one's own works and entering God's rest through faith in Christ.",

    "Genesis 2:2-3 (God rests on the seventh day and blesses it)",
    "Exodus 20:8-11 (Sabbath command grounded in creation rest)",
    "Deuteronomy 5:12-15 (Sabbath tied to redemption from Egypt)",
    "Hebrews 4:1-11 (a 'Sabbath rest remains for the people of God'; entering God's rest by faith)",
    "Matthew 11:28-30 (Christ's invitation, 'I will give you rest')",
    "Colossians 2:16-17 (Sabbaths as 'a shadow of things to come; the substance is Christ')",
    "Hebrews 3:7-19 (Israel's failure to enter rest as warning/type)"
  ],

        "Exodus 31:13-17",
        "Ezekiel 20:12, 20"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Transfer/creation-ordinance view (Reformed/Puritan sabbatarianism): the Sabbath is a perpetual moral command from creation, its symbolic and practical force transferred to the Lord's Day (Sunday) in honor of the resurrection.",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 2:2-3",
        "Exodus 20:8-11",
        "Acts 20:7",

        "Exodus 20:8-11",

        "Revelation 14:7, 12"

    {
      "meaning": "Millennial/cosmic-week typology (patristic): the seventh day prefigures a seventh 'millennial day' of world history or the world to come, as in the Epistle of Barnabas and some church fathers (also Augustine's 'eternal eighth day').",
      "basis": [
        "Genesis 2:2-3",
        "Psalm 90:4",
        "2 Peter 3:8",
        "Hebrews 4:9 (as read by patristic writers)"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"

    {
      "meaning": "Liberation/social-justice reading: the Sabbath as a symbol of release, humanitarian rest, and freedom from oppression and economic exploitation, tied to the exodus and jubilee patterns.",

        "Deuteronomy 5:12-15",
        "Exodus 23:12",
        "Leviticus 25 (sabbatical year and jubilee)",
        "Isaiah 58:13-14",
        "Luke 4:16-21; Luke 13:10-16 (Sabbath healings as release)"
      ],
      "prominence": "minority"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": true,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "There is broad, recognizable consensus across Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant interpretation that the Sabbath symbolizes rest in God, typologically fulfilled in Christ and consummated eschatologically (Hebrews 3-4 being the controlling text). Genuine disagreement lies not in the symbolism itself but in its practical entailments: whether a weekly observance continues (and on which day), which is where the Reformed sabbatarian, Lord's Day, and seventh-day traditions diverge. The covenant-sign, millennial-week, and liberation readings are usually treated as complementary layers rather than rivals to the 'rest in Christ' meaning."
}

BOOK ENTRY
The complete seven — six-and-one as a single whole, at every scale the law counts it: the week whose seventh day is the rest, the seventh year that rests the land, the seven-sevens that ring in jubilee. Scripture counts “seven sabbaths complete” and calls the week itself the sabbath; the rest-day is the crown of the unit, one-seventh of what the word names.

AVAILABLE KJV EXCERPTS
Leviticus 23:15 — And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete:
Leviticus 25:2 — Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the LORD.
Leviticus 25:3 — Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof;
Leviticus 25:4 — But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.
Leviticus 25:5 — That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap, neither gather the grapes of thy vine undressed: for it is a year of rest unto the land.
Leviticus 25:6 — And the sabbath of the land shall be meat for you; for thee, and for thy servant, and for thy maid, and for thy hired servant, and for thy stranger that sojourneth with thee,
Leviticus 25:7 — And for thy cattle, and for the beast that are in thy land, shall all the increase thereof be meat.
Leviticus 25:8 — And thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years; and the space of the seven sabbaths of years shall be unto thee forty and nine years.
2 Chronicles 36:21 — To fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.
Luke 18:12 — I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
Matthew 28:1 — In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
Hebrews 4:9 — There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.

CLASSIFY THE RELATIONSHIP

First reduce both readings to their minimum core identifications. Do not let
extra detail create an artificial disagreement.

- MATCH: the core identifications are equivalent. Differences are merely
  wording or immaterial detail.
- REFINED: the book preserves the consensus's general referent or category but
  materially changes its extension, boundary, conditions, or precision. A
  narrowing may reject some cases the broader consensus admits; a broadening
  may admit cases it excludes. This is real disagreement at the boundary, but
  not replacement of the central referent.
- DIVERGENT: the cores materially contradict. Both claims cannot be true of the
  same referent in the same context and sense; accepting the book requires
  rejecting or replacing the consensus identification. A source and its
  product remain different referents when the book explicitly denies their
  identity, even if they are causally related.
- NOVEL: no recognizable consensus or listed alternative covers the book's
  core identification. Novelty is absence from consensus, not contradiction.

Use `core_relation` to expose the relationship at the center and
`extension_relation` to expose disagreement over the cases covered. A REFINED
verdict must state what cases the book adds, excludes, or reclassifies. A
DIVERGENT verdict must identify a replaced referent or material contradiction,
not merely a narrower boundary.

Treat the two axes independently. A core-divergent reading may still retain
some cases covered by the consensus while rejecting its central identification;
therefore DIVERGENT does not require disjoint extensions. Conversely, a
narrowed extension is REFINED only when the consensus's central referent or
category remains intact.

Also judge whether the citations printed with the glossary entry alone provide
strong, partial, or insufficient support. Do not yet decide whether a divergent
full chapter is persuasive; that is a separate stage.
